name: Fit Constrained Deconvolution Model for Tracking
summary: Fits constrained spherical deconvolution (CSD) models to DWI with MRtrix3, using a T1-weighted image for a 5-tissue-type mask, and outputs fibre orientation distributions for one or more lmax values plus the 5TT and brain masks.
description: Converts the DWI to MRtrix format, builds a brain mask with FSL bet (or uses the provided brainmask) and a 5-tissue-type image with 5ttgen fsl (or uses the provided 5TT mask), then estimates response functions (dwi2response tournier for single-shell, msmt_5tt for multi-shell) and fits CSD/MSMT-CSD FODs with dwi2fod. Use it to produce the CSD input needed by MRtrix3 tracking Apps. With ensemble enabled it writes every even lmax up to the requested maximum; the requested lmax is capped at the maximum the data supports. Optional multi-tissue intensity normalisation uses mtnormalise.

inputs.description: The path to the DWI datatype
The path to the mask datatype of the brainmask for the DWI
The path to the mask datatype of the 5 tissue probability mask from Tissue-type Segmentation (optional). If not inputted, will be generated using MRtrix3
The path to the anat/t1w datatype

outputs.description: The 5 tissue probability image generated using MRtrix3
The brainmask of the DWI image

parameters.description: spherical harmonic order (lmax) for csd estimation. see https://mrtrix.readthedocs.io/en/3.0_rc2/constrained_spherical_deconvolution/lmax.html for more information on which value to choose
If T1 has been skull stripped, select true
if true, will ensemble through max lmax. else, will generate requested lmax

citations.text: Tournier J-D, Calamante F, Connelly A. Robust determination of the fibre orientation distribution in diffusion MRI: non-negativity constrained super-resolved spherical deconvolution. NeuroImage 35:1459-1472 (2007).

Jeurissen B, Tournier J-D, Dhollander T, Connelly A, Sijbers J. Multi-tissue constrained spherical deconvolution for improved analysis of multi-shell diffusion MRI data. NeuroImage 103:411-426 (2014).
